I am old now, and my legs are not what they used to be, but I still know this land. Beans do not need expensive chemicals from the shop—they make their own nitrogen, and my small plot is too little to waste money on such things. I will use manure from our goats like my mother taught me, and I will save my own seed from last season because it has always grown well here. My grandchildren will help me weed when the rains come, and we will manage with our own hands.
